text: "Breakfast is the most important meal of the day." Guess who said it first?
Not a doctor. A health magazine, printed in 1917...
...at the resort of the man who co-invented corn flakes.
Then, in the 1920s, a meatpacker hired a PR man to sell more bacon.
He didn't buy ads. He asked one doctor: light breakfast, or heavy? "Heavy."
Then that doctor wrote to five thousand physicians.
About 4,500 agreed. At least, that's how he told it.
Newspapers ran it. And the heartiest breakfast? Bacon and eggs.
The doctors never picked the menu. The bacon seller did. And, he said, his sales went up.
Eat it or skip it. Just know who wrote the slogan.
